title: Fix packaging namespace pollution and release-surface drift

preflight.note: Stamped by `repopact new`; the work item was recorded before implementation began.

acceptance_criteria.text: The published distribution installs exactly one top-level import name (a real `repopact` package) plus the console script; no generic top-level modules (`frontmatter`, `doctor`, `new`, `takeover`, `init_repo`, ...) land in site-packages. Verified by an evidence run that inspects the built wheel's contents.

Seed schemas and templates ship as package data resolved via importlib.resources; the deprecated setuptools data-files mechanism is removed. `repopact init` and `repopact adopt` work from a wheel install in a clean venv (evidence run, at minimum on Windows).

The validator enforces release-surface parity: the README release line must state the current VERSION and its changelog link must resolve to the matching release decision record. The current README (2.2.0 vs VERSION 2.3.0) is repaired and a regression test covers the rule.
ROADMAP.md no longer claims the `proposed` lifecycle state is unreleased (it shipped in 2.1.0); its 'Now' section reflects the 2.3.0 line.
Test-suite wall time is profiled and reduced from ~5.5 minutes to under 2 minutes locally (shared bootstrap fixtures instead of per-test init/adopt), or a decision records why the cost is accepted.
